mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which typically leads to higher consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of months when PAYEMS increases by at least 100k over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 0.25% for three consecutive months, it signals the Federal Reserve is initiating a tightening cycle, which typically causes a decline in equity valuations due to higher discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 24 months following FEDFUNDS exceeding 0.25% for 3 months, the S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 0.5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy in response to a tight labor market, which typically causes a sell-off in equities, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with monetary tightening
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE < 5% and FEDFUNDS > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market recovery (HOUST > 450k units), rising inflation (CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 0.2%) signals an overheating economy, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances during housing recovery with CPIAUCSL growth > 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates improving consumer confidence and economic activity, which typically leads to higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of months when HOUST increases by at least 5% over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 8.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a strengthening labor market that may lead to wage inflation and subsequent Federal Reserve tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 24 months following UNRATE falling below 8.5% for two months, the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) declines below 90 and real GDP growth (GDPC1) is negative for two consecutive quarters, it indicates a recessionary supply shock, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 90 AND GDPC1 quarterly growth rate < 0
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO < 90 and GDPC1 quarterly growth rate < 0.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL above 3.0% annualized), a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive monetary tightening, which typically causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL annualized inflation > 3.0% AND FEDFUNDS rising
failure_condition: In the 12 months following CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized with rising FEDFUNDS, the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
